items.title: GTA 6 leaks show a game that looks like more GTA, but not a revolution
items.summary: It sure doesn't look like the reinvention of the wheel(s).
items.body: The exciting thing about Rockstar games is not that they have the most advanced technology behind them, the best stories, or the most avant-garde game systems. It's the extraordinary amount of work the studio invests into the little details that make up its big worlds. Red Dead Redemption's dynamic horse testicles (they shrink when it's cold) are a frequently-cited example of that commitment to the particulars. A pair of videos purported to be leaked GTA 6 gameplay surfaced online today , and if they are legit (the immediate copyright takedowns suggest as much), they seem to confirm that GTA 6 is more of the same. The short clips obviously can't express the full scope of Rockstar's designs—and we don't know how recent they are—but there's nothing in them to indicate that GTA 6 will reinvent the open-world crime spree. His leading roles on games like Ultima Underworld , System Shock , and Deus Ex —and you know what, even Invisible War and Deadly Shadows , which are probably better than you think—established him as one of the field's most admired and enduring names. And now, after doing it for more than 40 years, he's calling it a day. "Let me cut right to the chase. I'm retiring from game development," Spector wrote on LinkedIn . "At least I think so. items.title: 'Live-service is a red flag for us': Why one publisher is embracing an older kind of multiplayer hit: peer-to-peer, server browsers, and organic community
items.summary: Tripwire sees preservation as a responsibility.
items.body: It's a frustrating thing to watch good games disappear. We've seen it happen time and time and time again: studios spend years on a cool multiplayer thing, bank on it being popular enough to become a live-service hit, then toss the entire project into the trash when that doesn't happen. That could have been the fate of Deceive Inc , a 2023 'PvP Hitman' shooter that has attracted a passionate, but small community. Developer Sweet Bandits supported the game with substantial updates and microtransactions for over a year, but unfortunately shut down in 2024, leaving fans to assume Deceive Inc would one day disappear, too. Then last month, the unexpected happened : an update on its Steam page announced that not only would Deceive Inc not be going offline, but work is underway on community server tools and mod support that will essentially give the game to the community, and keep it playable forever. The update is not the work of Sweet Bandits, but an initiative of Deceive Inc's publisher, Tripwire Interactive. items.title: Former PlayStation boss Shuhei Yoshida told Clair Obscur devs to not call it a 'turn-based RPG' so people wouldn't 'overlook' it
items.summary: More than eight million copies sold suggests he might've been right.
items.body: According to former PlayStation boss Shuhei Yoshida, turn-based RPGs, particularly JRPGs, were so unpopular several years ago that he would tell indie developers to avoid using the term altogether in their marketing—even for a game like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Yoshida recalled giving the Clair Obscur developers this advice during a lecture at the Busan Indie Connect Festival 2026 (via Automaton ). He was impressed by a demo he played a couple of years before the game was out, particularly its similarities to The Legend of Dragoon, a game he produced, but recommended the developers at Sandfall Interactive find alternative ways to describe its combat. "It's incredibly well-made, but it would be better not to call it a turn-based RPG," he said. "That alone might cause players to overlook it." Sandfall listened and started describing Clair Obscur's combat as "reactive turn-based battles" in its marketing. It's hard to tell if that actually had an impact on the breakout success of the game, but it probably didn't hurt. items.summary: نجم الوسط الإسباني يختار رقم قميصه مع البارسا
items.body: نجم الوسط الإسباني يختار رقم قميصه مع البارسا اختار رودري، لاعب وسط برشلونة الجديد، رقم قميصه مع الفريق الكتالوني، استعدادًا لبدء مشواره مع الفريق في الموسم الجديد. وأعلن برشلونة في وقت سابق من اليوم الثلاثاء ضم رودري رسميًا قادمًا من مانشستر سيتي بعقد يمتد حتى عام 2030. ويرتدي رودري القميص رقم 16 مع البارسا، ليعود لاعب الوسط الإسباني إلى رقم ارتبط به خلال محطات مهمة من مسيرته الاحترافية. وحسب صحيفة " سبورت "، جاء اختيار رودري لهذا الرقم بعد قرار فيرمين لوبيز تغيير قميصه، والانتقال إلى الرقم 7 الذي أصبح متاحًا عقب رحيل فيران توريس إلى باريس سان جيرمان. وكان فيرمين عبّر عن حزنه للتخلي عن الرقم الذي ارتداه خلال سنواته الأولى مع الفريق الأول. ووفقًا لـ"سبورت"، يحمل الرقم 16 أهمية خاصة في مسيرة رودري، بعدما ارتداه في فترات مختلفة مع فياريال ومانشستر سيتي، إلى جانب المنتخب الإسباني. ويعوّل هانز فليك على رودري ليكون أحد أبرز ركائز برشلونة، مستفيدًا من خبرته وقدراته في تنظيم اللعب والسيطرة على وسط الملعب، في صفقة يأمل النادي أن تمنحه التوازن الذي يبحث عنه. اقرأ أيضًا: فليك: رودري الأفضل في مركزه.. وهذه أبرز مميزاته

items.title: يبدأ من الصفر.. وكيل جودتس يكشف دور إنريكي في كواليس الانضمام لسان جيرمان
items.summary: أوضح نيلز دي يونك، وكيل أعمال البلجيكي ميكا جودتس، كواليس انضمامه إلى باريس سان جيرمان، رغم اهتمام أندية أخرى مثل برشلونة وبايرن ميونخ بخدماته.
items.body: أوضح نيلز دي يونك، وكيل أعمال البلجيكي ميكا جودتس، كواليس انضمامه إلى باريس سان جيرمان، رغم اهتمام أندية أخرى مثل برشلونة وبايرن ميونخ بخدماته. وأعلن سان جيرمان رسميًا يوم السبت الماضي، تعاقده مع جودتس، قادمًا من أياكس أمستردام بعقد حتى عام 2031. وصرح دي يونك، لصحيفة "دي تليجراف" الهولندية: " يعرف باريس سان جيرمان ميكا منذ صغره. والاهتمام الجاد الذي أبدته أندية مرموقة مثل أياكس آنذاك وباريس سان جيرمان الآن ليس مفاجئًا بالتأكيد". أكد دي يونك بشكل خاص تأثير لويس إنريكي مدرب سان جيرمان في القرار النهائي، مضيفًا حسبما نقلت شبكة " فوت ميركاتو ": " كان الحديث ودودًا للغاية منذ البداية، مليئًا بروح الدعابة، ولكنه ركز أيضًا، بالطبع، على الجوانب الجادة والرياضية". وتابع: "إنريكي يُقدّر اللاعبين متعددي المراكز، القادرين على التحرك في جميع أنحاء الملعب، وإيجاد المساحات، وخلق عنصر المفاجأة". وأكمل تصريحاته قائلًا: "أوضح باريس لميكا أن اهتمامهم جاد للغاية. لقد قدموا مشروعًا رياضيًا واضحًا، واستثمرت فيه شخصيات مهمة داخل النادي شخصيًا". مع ذلك، أراد دي يونك تحذير لاعبه: "إنه يبدأ من الصفر هناك. لكن على ميكا أن يثبت جدارته بمكانه في التشكيلة الأساسية. في نادٍ مثل باريس سان جيرمان، لا شيء مجاني. حتى في صفقة انتقال تُقدّر بحوالي 55 مليون يورو".

items.body: Two seemingly genuine Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay clips are making the rounds online. The first, a minute-long clip originally posted by a group or individual named "Cyberleek", is already being reposted in multiple places, but we first noticed it via gaming forum ResetEra . As of writing, the clip already has more than 100,000 views. In the clip, we see protagonist Jason Duval at an oceanside house—the same one that we've seen in trailers. The player jumps over his deck and onto the driveway, where he picks up a basketball and shoots some hoops. For sinking a basket, the player increases their "Focus" by 2%. We see two cash totals listed in the HUD—presumably one for their on-hand cash, and one for their bank. Another clip, posted almost an hour later, shows the player driving around a beat-up car, crashing into a delivery truck, and then attacking the driver. Elsewhere, Cyberleek has also published supposed screenshots of the in-game map, though art has appears too simple to be how it will actually look in the game. items.title: Epic Mickey creator Warren Spector is 'a little bitter' that his studio isn't getting props for sparking Oswald the Lucky Rabbit's big comeback
items.summary: Oswald, who featured in both Epic Mickey games, is getting an animated miniseries in 2027, and Spector rightly thinks his team should get credit for helping make it happen.
items.body: Epic Mickey man Warren Spector—also known for other games you may have heard of, like Ultima Underworld, System Shock, and Deus Ex—recently took to LinkedIn to share some thoughts about Disney's upcoming Oswald the Lucky Rabbit miniseries, which was showcased by Jon Favreau at the recent D23 event. Spector said he's "seriously looking forward to it," but he's also a little annoyed by what he sees as the erasure of the game that helped bring the character back into the public consciousness. Favreau provided a brief overview of Oswald's creation in the 1920s during his presentation, relating how creator Walt Disney lost the rights to the character shortly thereafter. While numerous Oswald shorts were produced, the character was utterly overshadowed by Disney's subsequent creation, Mickey Mouse, and languished in obscurity for years. Disney reacquired the rights to Oswald in 2006, and "we've seen him pop up in games and in shorts and things" since then, Favreau said—and, well, that's the extent of it. items.title: I modded GTA 5 into a life-sim RPG with mining, foraging, a mini-economy, and the ability to fall asleep in the middle of the road
items.summary: Which is what it's always been missing.
items.body: Grand Theft Auto 6 will, I'm assured, be the most immersive videogame of all time. You simply won't be able to discern reality from fiction anymore. Your gaze will drift from your television, to outside, to the television, to outside, and the sheer fidelity of Rockstar's opus will be such that you can no longer tell the slightest difference between the two. You will utterly lose your mind. It's gonna be great. GTA 5, though? Hardly immersive at all by comparison. If I'm going to successfully mod this game into GTA 6, I'm going to need to rectify that. So I did. items.summary: Make me use my noggin, please.
items.body: The humble combo trial is a time-honoured tradition in fighting games. It's a quick and relatively easy way of trying out a new character, feeling out their general flow and kit in a low-pressure environment. They are, also, fundamentally useless. The combos in question are rarely optimal, and often devolve into simply playing Simon Says a dozen times before throwing yourself to the wolves of online matchmaking and hoping for the best. I can't speak for anyone else, but I rarely retain any of the stuff I pick up during combo trials, and usually end up defaulting to the likes of Dustloop or trusted YouTube tutorials to figure out how to actually play a character. In the back-most pages of its 22nd issue, it tucked away an ad for a then-new game called Capitalism .
